Getúlio Vargas. The Brazilian military officer and politician who dominated Brazilian politics for twenty-four years, serving as president during both democratic and authoritarian periods. He modernized Brazil's economy and labour system while establishing a paternalistic, populist style of governance.

Vargas led a military coup in 1930 and took power, beginning the Vargas Era that would last until 1954. In 1937, he established the Estado Novo, or New State, a fascist-influenced authoritarian regime that lasted until 1945. He implemented labour reforms including the minimum wage, workers' compensation, and a labour code modeled on Italian fascism. Initially, Vargas supported Nazi Germany and Vichy France, but switched allegiance to the Allies in World War II. After losing power, he returned democratically in 1950, but faced mounting political pressures. In 1954, while still president, he committed suicide. Though his legacy remains controversial due to his authoritarianism, Vargas stayed popular among the working class and left an indelible mark on Brazilian politics.
